name: Unnamed Cargo Pants (Patched)
description: No-brand cargo pants that have been repaired so many times the original fabric is almost a minority. Patches in denim, synth-canvas, and heat-fused mylar strips cover the knees, seat, and inner thighs. The pockets still work — all six of them — which is the only thing that matters in the Gray Zone.
what_it_says: You've been surviving longer than most. These pants have a history and so do you.
story_hooks: A hidden inner pocket contains a folded note in a language the current owner doesn't read.
The patch on the left knee is cut from a Tier 4 corporate uniform — someone's past is stitched in.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian silhouette dominated by visible patchwork across the lower body. The pants read as functional salvage—multiple fabric types create an intentional chaos aesthetic. Worn by Tier 5 workers who prioritize durability over aesthetics.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through hip and thigh with a straight leg. Designed for movement and layering of protective gear. Not fitted; allows for cargo and the constant repositioning of worn patches.
physical_description.primary_material: Base layer appears to be standard work-grade cotton twill, now mostly obscured by overlays of repaired synth-canvas, denim scraps, and heat-fused mylar strips.
physical_description.texture: Heavily textured and tactile—rough twill base broken by smoother denim patches, crinkled mylar sections that catch light, and visible stitch lines from hand or crude machine repairs. Areas between patches show fraying and worn nap.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded indigo base with navy and medium blue denim patches. Translucent amber and silver mylar strips add reflective accents. The overall palette is muted and weathered, with no intentional color coordination.
physical_description.closures: Worn brass button fly, likely original. Heavy-gauge zipper shows corrosion but functions. No belt loops—cargo belt worn separately.
distinctive_features: Six functional cargo pockets—thigh, hip, and side panels
Prominent patching at knees (double-layered synth-canvas), seat (mylar-reinforced), and inner thighs (mixed denim)
Visible mending lines and irregular stitching patterns
Heat-fused mylar reflects ambient light, marking repair zones
Frayed cuff edges and worn hem from constant foot drag
Small burn marks and chemical stains suggesting shelf-work exposure
Original garment label removed or worn away
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade. No branding, purely functional. The patchwork itself signals someone who cannot afford replacement and must sustain gear through improvisation.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by autonomous machine handlers, shelf workers, or independent salvagers in ungoverned sectors. Signals practical competence, resourcefulness, and comfort with hand-maintenance. No corpo affiliation. This is clothing that has earned its scars.
physical_description.condition_typical: Always patched and weathered. Condition improves slightly mid-shift when new patches are applied. Never pristine. The wearer considers this optimal—the more patches, the more valuable the garment.
